title: introduce-commitment-smoothing-escrow-and-tenant-earnings-meter
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleet tenants sometimes experience oscillation between conservative reservation and aggressive bursting. This leads to unpredictable tail latency and surprising billing spikes for customers. This PR introduces a two-part system: (1) a sliding-window commitment smoother that reduces abrupt reservation changes by computing a stable committed throughput per-tenant using a configurable EWMA-like window and quantile smoothing, and (2) an escrow-backed tenant earnings meter that accrues unused reservation headroom as "earnings" which can be consumed for short bursts. The escrow enforces safety caps so burst consumption cannot exceed a configured multiple of the committed baseline and supports soft-reclamation when global headroom is scarce. Design summary:
 - window_commitment.go: implements a sliding-window commitments calculator. It tracks per-tenant request-rate histograms over a rolling 10-minute window (configurable) and exposes a 95th percentile commitment with hysteresis thresholds to avoid frequent flips. The smoother has two knobs: smoothing_half_life (seconds) and commit_quantile (e.g., 0.95).
 - escrow_controller.go: standalone controller that maintains an on-disk escrow ledger for each tenant (durable CRD-backed entries) and a volatile in-memory balance to optimize decision latency. The ledger stores "earnings" (tokens proportional to unused committed capacity) and enforces per-tenant caps: max_escrow_ratio and emergency_reclaim_ratio.
 - tenant CRD changes: api/v1alpha1/tenant_commitment_types.go adds fields (commitmentSmoothing, escrowConfig) to allow per-tenant tuning and migration defaults.
 - Observability: new metrics (redwood_commitment_committed_tpm, redwood_escrow_balance_tokens, redwood_escrow_spend_rate, redwood_escrow_reclaim_events) with labels (tenant_id, region) and dashboards added to the docs.
 - Rollout and safety: default behavior off for existing tenants; opt-in via tenant CRD. Escrow spending is conservative by default (max_escrow_ratio=1.5) and includes circuit breakers that will deny spending when cluster-wide free capacity < reclamation_threshold.
Tests and validation:
 - unit tests for commitment smoothing math and quantile calculation.
 - integration e2e test escrow_e2e_test.go simulates tenants with alternating low/high load and asserts earnings accumulate and are spent only within configured caps.
 - performance smoke tests to verify the controller loop adds <3ms p99 CPU overhead per reconciler cycle in a synthetic test.
Migration and data safety: ledger entries are stored as CRDs with finalizers and safe reconcile loops to avoid double-spend. The scripts/seed-tenant-credits.sh provides an administrative helper to bootstrap earnings for tenants that migrated from older reservation systems. Related work: ties into ENG-2138 (autoscaler stability follow-up) and ENG-2179 (tenant billing telemetry). This PR is intentionally conservative in defaults and includes a gradual rollout plan described below. Configuration knobs:
 - smoothing_half_life: "300s" default
 - commit_quantile: "0.95" default
 - max_escrow_ratio: "1.5" default
 - emergency_reclaim_ratio: "0.3" default
 - min_balance_for_spend: "10" tokens.
Rollout plan:
 1) Merge behind feature flag (manager flag --enable-escrow).
 2) Enable for internal staging tenants and run 48h soak with traffic replay.
 3) Gradual opt-in for customers: enable by adding the tenant CRD fields.
 4) Monitor new metrics for 7 days, watch for reclaim events.
 5) Tweak defaults based on observed cluster-wide utilization.
Backwards compatibility: existing tenants not specifying the new fields will behave identically post-merge. Documentation: docs/runbooks/commitment-escrow.md contains runbook steps for enabling, debugging, and emergency reclaim. CI notes: (see checks) The initial e2e run timed out on the first try due to a flaky environment; subsequent runs passed. Merge notes: squash-merged into main after approvals.

review_comments: Sofia Park: Please add an integration test that verifies emergency reclaim will not push cluster into overcommit - requested change.
Maya Chen: Added e2e scenario that simulates reclaim under constrained cluster capacity and asserts no tenant gets negative balance (see escrow_e2e_test.go) - reply.
Ethan Cole: Could we expose smoothing_half_life as a Helm override? Also asked for runtime feature flag in manager - requested change.
Maya Chen: Exposed smoothing_half_life via helm and added --enable-escrow flag to manager. Confirmed with smoke test on staging - reply.
Priya Nair: Approve after addressing metrics label cardinality concern (limit tenant_id usage to dashboards only).
Sofia Park: Approved - safety knobs look sane and migration path is clear.
release_notes: Introduces opt-in commitment smoothing and an escrow-based tenant earnings meter. Defaults are conservative and feature is disabled unless enabled via tenant CRD or manager flag. Adds new telemetry metrics for commitment and escrow balances.
